brief.title: CUT — a first collection
brief.audience: Buyers, press, and two stockists at a preview breakfast
brief.objective: Place a first order, and understand that the collection is nine pieces and will stay nine pieces
brief.visualDirection: Authored for this deck; see creativeDirection.
brief.sourcePrompt: Showcase brief: CUT — a first collection

narrative: By the end a buyer should place an order, because the range is deliberately small and the reason it is small is the product.

alternatives.name: Wall text
alternatives.thesis: A gallery wall: type at architectural scale, one plate per room, labels that behave like labels
alternatives.differentiator: Type is the composition. Words run off the edge of the page; the plates never carry a caption on the same slide

alternatives.name: Line sheet
alternatives.thesis: The nine pieces as a priced grid, the way a buyer will see them in a showroom
alternatives.differentiator: Regular grid, small images, dense data
alternatives.rejectedBecause: A line sheet is what the follow-up email is for; the room is for deciding the collection is worth stocking

creativeDirection.name: Wall text
creativeDirection.concept: A gallery wall rather than a line sheet: the type is the object and the plates are hung, not captioned
creativeDirection.rationale: The collection's argument is restraint, and a dense priced grid argues the opposite before anyone reads a word
creativeDirection.geometryLanguage: No containers at all. One hairline baseline per slide, and type that is allowed to run off the edge
creativeDirection.spatialRhythm: Alternating: a page of type, then a plate, and never two plates together
creativeDirection.materialLanguage: Undyed wool and gallery paint; a single cut of red used exactly twice in the deck

plate.description: One image, full height, never captioned on the same slide

bleed.description: Type that runs off the top or side edge
bleed.meaning: The collection is larger than the page

hard: No slide carries both a plate and a price
Every price on the deck is wholesale, ex-VAT, and says so
soft: Labels are always tracked and always grey

avoid: more than two colours per slide

title: CUT
designIntent: One word at architectural scale, bleeding off the top edge. Everything else is at label size.
composition: An enormous word occupying the upper page and running past the top edge; three labels at the foot.

text: Nine pieces in one cloth. The range is small because the cloth is, and both of those are the argument.

notes: Let the word sit for a few seconds before saying anything.

title: The cloth
designIntent: Show the cloth before naming a price. No caption on this slide — the label is the whole text.
composition: A full-height plate on the right two-thirds; a single tracked label at the lower left.

alt: A hard diagonal edge dividing pale cloth from deep shadow

provenance.source: Abstract cloth study generated for this showcase; not a photograph of a garment

text: One mill, one weight, one finish. Every piece in the collection is cut from it.

notes: Pass the swatch round here, not later.

title: Nine
designIntent: The constraint as a numeral. It is the only slide with a single word on it and that is the point.
composition: A numeral filling the left half; one line of type beneath the baseline.

text: Nine pieces, and it stays nine. Nothing is added mid-season, nothing is dropped, and the second delivery is the same nine in the same cloth.

notes: This is the commitment buyers will test. Say it plainly.

title: The nine
designIntent: Name them without making a catalogue. One block of names, set as text, not as a grid.
composition: A single dense block of names occupying the middle band, in two columns.

text: THE COAT · THE SHORT COAT · THE OVERSHIRT · THE TROUSER · THE WIDE TROUSER · THE SKIRT · THE DRESS · THE SCARF · THE BAG
Sizes 1–4 across all nine. The bag and the scarf are one size and are the only pieces not cut from the coat cloth.

notes: Do not read the list aloud. Let them read it.

title: Terms
designIntent: The commercial slide. No plate, no price on the same page as an image — that is a hard constraint of this deck.
composition: A table low on the page under a title, with the upper third deliberately empty.

rows: 2.4× cost at the quoted mill price

text: Every figure here is wholesale and ex-VAT. The costing sheet is in the follow-up.

notes: No pictures on this slide on purpose. Prices and plates never share a page.

sources.label: Internal costing sheet, first production run

title: Order by 30 April
designIntent: Two lines at the foot of an empty page. The deck stops where the conversation starts.
composition: An empty upper page; one instruction and one date across the lower band.

text: Order by 30 April for the August drop.
After that the mill's minimum has already been placed and the second drop is the earliest date.

notes: The mill deadline is real. It is why the date is the date.
